editorial.headline: Company Training for the People Who Keep a Home Running
editorial.standfirst: A company-run training activity for domestic work roles, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity covers company-organised job training intended to build practical skills for domestic work: household management, elder care, infant and toddler care, childcare, cooking, and related roles. Its subject is not the household service itself, but the structured training that prepares people for it. That distinction gives the activity a clear professional centre of gravity: developing capability for work that is intimate, practical, and often essential to daily family life.

The organiser is a company delivering that training. The record presents a broad occupational field rather than a narrow single-role programme, allowing the activity to encompass instruction for several forms of domestic work within the same company-led training setting. It does not state any business-scale categories open to this activity, so the record offers no basis for attaching a particular scale requirement or market tier to the registration.

Nationally, the activity is marked open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Put another way, the national record permits this activity to be owned entirely by foreign investors. The relevant national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That openness matters because it frames the business as a legitimate foreign-investment proposition at the national level, rather than one whose foreign participation is already limited by a stated ownership cap.

Bali’s position requires its own reading. The activity is marked as OK or higher risk and is not blocked by the provincial moratorium. The record explains that medium-high and high-risk activities are not blocked by that moratorium, while also directing applicants to verify the position for the specific address. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA restriction applies to all low and medium-low risk activities; this record does not place this activity in that blocked category. A foreign investor therefore has a genuinely open national route and no stated Bali moratorium block here, but should verify the address-specific position before treating a Bali location as settled.
